pages.meta_description: For ten years, Ricochet has helped professional and trade associations grow membership, revenue and impact through marketing, technology and data.
pages.text: About Ricochet Ricochet works only with associations. For ten years, Ricochet has helped professional and trade associations grow membership, revenue and impact through marketing, technology and data. Want to talk it through? Meet with us Leadership Who leads the work? Chris Gloede, MBA, CAE Chief Consultant Before Ricochet, Chris served as the first Chief Marketing Officer of the American Bar Association, where he grew membership to its highest count in 137 years. Before the ABA, he worked at Ogilvy and Leo Burnett, driving marketing experiments for brands such as BP, Chrysler, Kraft and Unilever. Today he teaches live classes for association executives at the Association Academy. Chris holds the CAE credential and an MBA from the University of Chicago Booth School of Business. He once traveled for 53 weeks through 48 countries and 118 cities, chasing architecture and history. Connect with Chris on LinkedIn The team Who will I work with? Most of the Ricochet team worked inside associations before working for them, so they understand volunteer governance and mission-driven decisions. Tom Felgar, MBA Solution Engineer Tom has spent more than 15 years helping associations, nonprofits and schools adopt new marketing technology. He leads HubSpot implementations and their ongoing evolution. He previously worked at the American Academy of Dermatology and the American Bar Association, and he is a HubSpot Certified Trainer. Laura Aguilar Analyst and Producer Laura brings international digital marketing experience from B2B and B2C companies. At Ricochet she supports HubSpot implementation, marketing automation and design, and she leads production of the Association Academy courses. Chelsea Forgille Consultant Chelsea leads project management at Ricochet, carrying complex initiatives from kickoff to completion. She previously ran membership campaigns and marketing automation at the American Bar Association. Stacy Jeziorowski Consultant Stacy has more than 15 years in association marketing and communications. She led a full rebrand as Marketing and Communications Lead at the Computer Science Teachers Association, and at Ricochet she leads client membership and event strategy and campaigns. Fernando Velarde Creative Director Fernando brings two decades of UI/UX architecture and web design. He delivers branding and design at speed, and he led design for major summits including CERF 2025 and the SACUBO Annual Meeting. Explore Where else can I get to know Ricochet? pages.meta_description: Facing its first major dues increase in years, AAO-HNS used tested renewal messaging from Ricochet and exceeded its revenue goals.
pages.text: Marketing Studio case study AAO-HNS Creates a Bold Plan for Membership Renewal Facing its first major dues increase in years, AAO-HNS worked with Ricochet on tested renewal messaging and materials, exceeding revenue goals with minimal member complaints. What was holding AAO-HNS back? The American Academy of Otolaryngology-Head and Neck Surgery (AAO-HNS) has approximately 13,000 members. After years of stable rates, it needed to raise dues significantly, which meant core physician members would pay over $1,000. The organization knew the move was risky. Without a solid communication strategy, it could face backlash at renewal time. AAO-HNS partnered with Ricochet to handle the change with care. What did Ricochet do? Ricochet wrote a range of messaging options and researched them with AAO-HNS members to find which ones might draw negative feedback. With those findings, we guided the marketing team on the wording and design of renewal emails. We fully redesigned the printed and faxed renewal materials and worked with the printer and mailer on production. We set clear targets for the campaign and built a real-time view so staff could monitor progress as renewals came in. What changed for AAO-HNS's members? Members received renewal emails and printed materials with wording that had been tested with their peers before it went out. The dues increase reached them with a clear explanation instead of a surprise. Complaints from members about the higher dues were minimal, and AAO-HNS exceeded its revenue goals for the renewal campaign, setting it up for continued growth. pages.text: Membership Modeling case study AAPA Grows With Tiered Membership AAPA had approved a tiered membership model but lacked the staff to roll it out, so Ricochet led a year-long implementation that hit its revenue goals. What was holding AAPA back? The American Academy of Physician Associates (AAPA) has more than 74,000 members. After careful research, AAPA concluded that membership tiers with different benefits and rates could increase revenue, and its leadership approved the change. There was a hitch. AAPA did not have the staff to handle everything the new model required across its systems and departments. It hired Ricochet to lead the work. What did Ricochet do? Ricochet led a year-long project to put the new membership model in place. This was a major overhaul. We coordinated a large team drawn from multiple departments. On the technical side, the work included changes to the association management system and the learning management system. On the financial side, the ledger had to be updated. We also covered member-facing pieces, including communications and customer care scripts. What changed for AAPA's members? AAPA members can now choose from membership tiers that offer different benefits at different rates, instead of a single offering. Because communications and customer care scripts were updated alongside the systems, members heard a consistent explanation of the new tiers when they reached out. AAPA launched the tiers successfully and hit its revenue goals with precision. pages.text: Tech and AI Roadmaps case study ACEP Translates Its Technology Strategy into a Roadmap Ricochet turned ACEP's ambitious technology strategy into a five-year roadmap, with new systems phased in to limit disruption and detailed projections of upfront and ongoing costs. What was holding ACEP back? The American College of Emergency Physicians (ACEP) serves more than 38,000 members across emergency medicine. Another consultancy had written ACEP an ambitious strategic technology plan, but the plan did not explain how to reach its vision. ACEP needed a roadmap, not just a destination. It partnered with Ricochet to turn the strategy into manageable changes it could carry out. What did Ricochet build? Ricochet evaluated ACEP's current systems to see which fit the planned future. The team found a need for new learning management, financial management, association management and marketing solutions. Because too much change at once could overwhelm staff, Ricochet set a five-year timeline that accounts for how the systems will work together and keeps disruption to daily operations low. Ricochet also organized demos with leading association software providers and built projections of upfront and ongoing costs. What changed for ACEP's members? Phasing new systems over five years aims to minimize disruption to ACEP's day-to-day operations and avoid overwhelming staff. The roadmap considered how the different solutions would work together. pages.text: HubSpot case study AOTA Transforms Marketing with HubSpot AOTA replaced an outdated email system with HubSpot Marketing Hub, with Ricochet finishing four project tracks in 14 weeks and overseeing AOTA's migration of over 400,000 records from its AMS into HubSpot. What was holding AOTA back? The American Occupational Therapy Association (AOTA) represents more than 244,500 occupational therapists, occupational therapy assistants and students. It wanted to change how it interacted with members, event attendees and customers, but its outdated email system stood in the way. AOTA selected HubSpot Marketing Hub to replace it and chose Ricochet to implement the new platform and train its staff. What did Ricochet build? Ricochet led the HubSpot implementation and completed four project tracks in just 14 weeks. We configured the system, including email templates, forms, automations, data hygiene and core technical settings. We oversaw AOTA's work to bring over 400,000 records from its AMS into HubSpot. We trained staff to pass the HubSpot Marketing Software Certification Exam. We also rebuilt the email preference center with new subscription categories and a stronger data privacy policy. What changed for AOTA's members? Members now manage their email through a revamped preference center with new subscription categories, backed by a stronger data privacy policy. Transportation Selection Employees will select reasonably-priced flight, train, or other providers that meet the travel requirements; employees will strive to book at least two weeks in advance. pages.text: Member Research How do I understand what my members need? Stop guessing. Field a member survey your board can trust, then act on what it tells you. Ricochet runs association member surveys from the first question to the final recommendation. What would change your plan? Meet with us How it works What happens in a member survey project? Four phases, each one feeding the next, from the research objectives to the last recommendation. Administration A kickoff workshop sets the research objectives, the segments and the roles. Weekly status meetings keep it on track. Discovery We review your past research and talk with staff and stakeholders, so the survey asks what you actually need to know. Fieldwork We write, design and program the survey, then send the invitations and reminders that drive response. Recommendations We analyze every response and deliver findings, each with a recommendation your team can act on. Why Ricochet What makes a Ricochet member survey different? Numbers your board can trust, cut the way your board thinks, with a next step attached to each one. Segments, then slices Every top-line number is cut by the segments your board worries about. Double and triple slices are standard, not an add-on, so one survey yields dozens of findings instead of one average. Statistical confidence on everything We report the confidence interval alongside every score. A 4 and a 3 are the same number until the interval says otherwise, so you never react to noise in a small subgroup. Every comment, coded AI makes open-ended answers analyzable at scale. Every comment is coded into themes, so hundreds of write-ins become a finding instead of a few quotes. Findings ship with action Every finding comes with a recommendation, sorted into easy wins your team can move on now and long-term initiatives that need budget or buy-in. What you get What do I get at the end of a member survey? A formal findings report your leaders can act on, with a recommendation for every finding. A survey built for your members The survey instrument, written and designed for you. Fielding handled for you Programming, invitations and reminders, managed by Ricochet. Every response analyzed Each result cut by segment and reported with its margin of error. Recommendations you can act on A findings and recommendations report, plus the full dataset. Free download What questions belong in a member survey? Survey findings often lead to the next step. Findings on dues feed Membership Modeling , and findings on perception feed the Marketing Studio . Methods Should I run a survey, focus groups or interviews? A survey is quantitative: it measures how many members hold a view. A focus group is qualitative: it explores why. Most associations start with a survey. Member survey Focus groups AI-assisted interviews Purpose Validate. Confirm what you believe, with the statistical confidence to set direction. Explore. Open, unstructured discussion that shapes ideas and feeds your decisions. Both. Open-ended exploration, at a scale that supports confidence. Answers How many members hold a view Why members feel the way they do How many, and why Who takes part Your whole membership (including prospects and past members.) 6 to 12 participants per group Hundreds of participants, each on their own schedule Statistically significant? Yes, reported by segment with confidence intervals No. Groups are too small. Yes, with enough participants Questions What associations ask about member surveys Do we need a survey or focus groups? + A survey validates: it tells you, with statistical confidence, how many members hold a view. Focus groups explore: open discussion that shapes ideas before you decide. Most associations start with a survey. What does a member survey cover? + Questions are ordered by what each one is worth: a loyalty score benchmarked against the industry, member benefits ranked by segment, questions on your current strategic initiatives, communication preferences, and demographics. Can you survey lapsed members and prospects? + Yes. Nonmember surveys reach lapsed members and prospects, so you learn why people leave and what would bring them in. What do we get at the end? + A formal report with a recommendation for every finding, split into easy wins and long-term initiatives, plus the full dataset for your permanent records. How many responses do we need? + Enough for each segment you want to compare. We report confidence intervals, so you know which differences are real and which are noise. What do members actually value? + Ask them, then cut the answer by segment. A member survey has members rate and rank each benefit, then compares the results across member types, career stages and regions. A benefit that ranks low overall can matter most to one segment. Ricochet reports each result with its margin of error, so you act on real differences, not noise. How do we get a real response rate on a member survey? + Keep it short enough to finish. Put the highest-value questions first, and pre-fill what your AMS already knows, such as member type and years of membership. Then send a planned series of invitations and reminders. Tiers charge different rates for substantially different benefits. What is a firm or group membership model? + One organization pays for a group of its people to join, instead of each person joining alone. We model how a group rate affects members, revenue and renewals. How do associations grow membership? + By pulling three levers together: the benefits members value, dues rates set against peers, and member types or tiers that fit each audience. How do you keep member data safe with AI? + Data protection is part of every roadmap. Each agent gets access only to the data it needs, and your team stays in control of it. What is an AI agent? + Software that carries out a routine task on its own, such as sorting an inbox or flagging duplicate records, and reports back to staff. Agents live in your own platforms, so your team owns them. How long does a technology roadmap take? + About 90 days from discovery to a roadmap and budget, with optional help building integrations and agents after that. Make one big change a year, so staff can absorb it, and connect and clean your member data first. A roadmap sets the timing and the five-year cost.
